judgments.reasoning: Independently read the transcript from 0 through 131 seconds and the catalogue chapters. At 31.72–58.6 the speaker introduces a synthetic fixture: equal underlying fraud by language, an English-centric description-quality score, and its addition because it improves overall detection. At 60.56–80.4, region flag rates of 9.2%, 9.1%, and 9.1% mask the language effect. At 80.4–101.4 the better aggregate fraud detection (33.5%) coexists with roughly one-fifth English-fraud detection, over 40% Hindi-fraud detection, and over half Hinglish-fraud detection. This concretely teaches f1; it does not teach slice denominators/counts, representativeness caveats, or NumPy mean/std, so f2–f5 are not confirmed. Tighten the opening from 31 to 32 seconds to begin with the new fixture explanation rather than the preceding lab teaser. Stop at 101 before the 101.4-second Model B feature-removal explanation (blocked mle.subgroup_risk_mitigation). Choosing dimensions from harm analysis at 76.92 is a recommendation, not a procedure the learner must understand to follow the rates. Catalogue chapters 'The region view shows nothing' and 'Where the better model catches fraud', the thumbnail reference, and the spoken side-by-side figures support inferred data-table teaching value, not directly verified frames. English auto-captions and embeddability are recorded. Partial mental-model coverage is intentional and sufficient for this short role; figures are synthetic, not production findings.

Independently read the entire 2286–2813 proposal plus approximately 30 seconds on each side and the catalogue logging/media chapters. At 2301.84–2377.92 the presenter makes lecture 4.py, imports MLflow, sets an experiment, and creates a named run. At 2409.12–2467.92 learning-rate/epoch parameters are hard-coded (0.03, 100, then differently named 0.04 and 200). At 2568.8–2626.96 accuracy values are illustrative 90 and 80, not computed validation results. At 2712.16–2759.6 a loss-graph image is searched for online and downloaded; it is not a diagnostic produced by the recorded experiment. The visible artifact result at 2789.04–2813.04 establishes generic file logging. Thus log_params, log_metric, and log_artifact API mechanics are partially demonstrated, but the only claimed fact f2 requires resolved configuration, validation results, and a diagnostic file belonging to that experiment. No complete claimed fact is confirmed. BLOCKING: the claimed experiment-evidence linkage is not taught; replace with a segment that logs actual resolved configuration, computed validation results, and a corresponding diagnostic artifact, or submit this only against a separately evidenced generic-logging fact. Boundary trimming cannot create that missing linkage. The run-ID experiment at 2484.24–2517.08 is corrected rather than left as an unsupported claim. Earlier local store/UI setup and lecture 1.py are referenced at 2672.16–2686.88, reducing standalone workflow clarity. Learning rate, epochs, and loss are merely names/context for values and a file; understanding optimizer configuration or training diagnosis is not needed for the logging mechanics, so this is not rejected for prerequisite leakage. Catalogue chapters, thumbnail reference and narrated file editing/UI inspection support inferred live-code value; frames were not inspected. Catalogue records English auto-captions and embeddability. ADVISORY: 527 seconds includes run-ID experimentation and image searching, making it poorly paced even though it completes the example.

Independently read 0–145 seconds, covering the proposed cut and its margins, and the catalogue chapters. The original 34-second opening still contains the API-token advertisement ('use the link in the description' at 33.04). Move to 35, the regularization chapter opening at 34.88. At 45.52–74 the speaker defines overfitting as fitting training data closely while failing to generalize and supplies a one-input/one-output fitted-curve example. At 74–111.52 the speaker compares validation loss and training loss: with more training, validation loss rises while training loss falls, showing overfitting. This teaches f1 with the same lower-is-better loss interpretation. It does not teach declared regularization-setting selection, error-rate denominators, expected cost, sealed test safeguards, or Ridge alpha/LogisticRegression C; f2–f6 are not confirmed. Stop at 115 after the transition question and before the new high-variance explanation at 115.52. Neural networks and epochs are passing context: 'train our model more and more' supplies the meaning needed for the comparison; neither network architecture, optimizer operation, nor a minibatch training loop must be understood. No prerequisite rejection is warranted. 'Look at this example' and the fitted-curve/loss comparison, together with the purpose-of-regularization chapter and thumbnail reference, support inferred signaled-slide teaching value, not verified frames. Catalogue records English auto-captions and embeddability. This is a useful partial mental model, not a complete selection workflow; downstream text must cover the unconfirmed facts.

Independently read 95–656 seconds, including the complete proposed range, and the custom-dataset/indexing/loader chapters. At 154.66–204.94 the speaker introduces Dataset inheritance, __init__, __getitem__(index), and __len__; 386.05–428.47 supplies sample count and returns self.x[index], self.y[index]. This teaches f1. At 497.57–550.88 DataLoader is configured with batch_size=4 and shuffle=True; at 597.35–626 the printed four feature vectors have corresponding labels, teaching f4. f2's list-based observation contract, f3's for-features-targets iteration, f5's incomplete-batch policy, and f6's assertions are not taught in this range. BLOCKING: at 568.31–581.9 the executable example retrieves the batch with data_iter.next(). Verified independently against the official PyTorch data tutorial (which uses next(iter(train_dataloader))) and v2.9.0 torch/utils/data/dataloader.py: _BaseDataLoaderIter defines __next__, not next. The demonstrated retrieval fails on the current API. Replace this demo with a current next(data_iter) or for-features-targets example; trimming away the faulty retrieval would also remove the runnable bridge to the claimed minibatch result, so the proposed coherent demo cannot be fixed by boundary adjustment. The training-loop simulation starts at 632.81 and is outside the proposal. Earlier batching/forward/backward language is outside the cut and is not needed to follow the in-range data operations, so no blocked training knowledge is required. ADVISORY: substantial Dataset subclass authoring at 154–434 lies beyond this path's supplied-scaffolding exercise boundary, and the 501-second cut spends much of its time on CSV/class setup. That is a scope/pacing concern, not independently a later-concept prerequisite blocker. Catalogue chapters, thumbnail reference, narrated code entry and printed tensors support inferred live-code visual value; frames were not inspected. Catalogue records English auto-captions and embeddability.
